newsitem.title: USA: Alexion drug's phase I/II trial successful.
newsitem.headline: Alexion drug's phase I/II trial successful.

text.p: Alexion Pharmaceuticals Inc said Monday its lead drug candidate, the C5 Inhibitor 5G1.1-SC, was well tolerated in a phase I/II trial, and showed biological efficacy in patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass.
Based on the results of that trial, Alexion has received authorization from the United States Food and Drug Administration to start a phase IIa clinical trial for cardiopulmonary bypass.

The phase IIa study will include up to 18 patients undergoing heart surgery at two clinical sites and is expected to gather additional information regarding the biological effects of certain doses compared to placebo.
The company said it plans to follow this study with a larger phase II study.
Alexion said the primary goal of the phase I/II clinical trial was to examine the safety of the drug candidate in patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass.

The drug was administered in a placebo-controlled manner to 17 patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass at one of four doses. The interim analysis shows that the drug was well tolerated by the study population, Alexion said.
Treatment with the drug candidate reduced the more than ten-fold increase in the level of activated complement byproducts experienced by patients on placebo during cardiopulmonary bypass.
